# Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

# Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1

```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

# Add in Data

Load libraries and data at the top of your document

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: fenced

# loading all libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# 2+2+2
# Reading in Data 
mydata <- mtcars
my_real_data <- read_csv("C:/Users/900117198/Desktop/ArcGIS/R/projects/scripts/Week7_DataViswggplot/data-visualizations-with-ggplot/data/sttstj_fish_biomass.csv")

#ORRR
my_real_data2 <- read_csv("../data/sttstj_fish_biomass.csv")

head(my_real_data2)


```

# Inserting figures and captions

```{r}
#| label: fig-mpg
#| fig-cap: "Figure 1. Scatterplot of Car Weight vs. MPG"


ggplot(mydata, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_minimal() + 
  labs( x = "Weight", y = "Miles Per Gallon")

```

::: callout-tip
## Tip

As shown in @fig-mpg, heavier cars typically have lower MPG

# Table Outputs

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| fig-cap: "Average MPG by Cylinder Count"

mydata |>
  group_by(cyl) |>
  summarise(avg_mpg = mean(mpg)) |>
  kable()
```

# Inserting Images

``` markdown
![](images/add.jpeg here){fig-algn="center" width=50% .lightbox}

fig-algn="center" - centers the image
width=50% - scaled the photo
.lightbox - when user clicks on the image full resolution pops up

![](images/add.jpeg here){fig-algn="center" width=50% .lightbox}
```
